Ibrahim (ClientCo): Hi team — over the last 48h we've got intermittent SSE streams from /v1/streams that terminate mid-JSON. Clients report JSON parse errors and our logs show finish_reason missing. Roughly 0.3% of sessions. Impacting chat freshness.
Claire (support): Sorry to hear that. Can you give a compact repro + the exact raw bytes you captured? Also which region and whether you're going through an ALB/Cloudfront?
Ibrahim (ClientCo): Using a Go http client inside our edge: we proxy the stream to browsers. Minimal repro (go):
```
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-chat", strings.NewReader(`{"prompt":"Hello","stream":true}`))
req.Header.Set("Authorization","Bearer SK_ABC")
req.Header.Set("Accept","text/event-stream")
resp, _ := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
for scanner.Scan() { fmt.Println(scanner.Text()) }
```
We saved a pcap and produced this hexdump of the final bytes (xxd -g1):
```
00000aa0: 64 61 74 61 3a 20 7b 22 69 64 22 3a 22 72 73 70  |data: {"id":"rsp|
00000ab0: 5f 31 32 33 22 2c 22 63 68 6f 69 63 65 73 22 3a  |_123","choices":|
00000ac0: 5b 7b 22 64 65 6c 74 61 22 3a 7b 22 63 6f 6e 74 65  |[{"delta":{"conte|
00000ad0: 6e 74 22 3a 22 e2 9c 93 20 54 68 61 74 27 73 20  |nt":"\xe2\x9c\x93 That's |
00000ae0: 20 61 20 64 72 61 66 74 2e 22 7d 5d 7d 0a 64 61 74  | a draft."}]}..dat|
00000af0: 61 3a 20 7b 22 69 64 22 3a 22 72 73 70 5f 31 32  |_a: {"id":"rsp_12|
00000b00: 33 22 2c 22 63 68 6f 69 63 65 73 22 3a 5b 7b 22 64  |3","choices":[{"d|
00000b10: 65 6c 74 61 22 3a 7b 22 63 6f 6e 74 65 6e 74 22 3a  |elta":{"content":"|
00000b20: 22 50 61 72 74 69 61 6c 20 64 61 74 61 20 63 75 74  |"Partial data cut|
00000b30: 2e 20 22 7d 5d 7d                                |. "}]}|
```
Then the connection closed (FIN). Note the UTF-8 checkmark character (0xE2 0x9C 0x93) appears in the first complete event but the next repeated block is cut before text finishes. No `data: [DONE]`.
Claire (support): Thanks  that's great detail. Do you see any 401/429/5xx prior? Any internal proxy (nginx) timeouts? Did the client receive any TCP RST?
Ibrahim (ClientCo): No errors in HTTP logs. We have an ALB in front of our edge plus nginx in the edge worker. From pcap I see FIN from server side, not RST. The close happens ~800ms after the last bytes.
deploy-bot: rolling deploy: stream-api v2026.11.01 at 2026-11-01T02:00:05Z
Zoe (runtime): Looking at the pattern: duplicated prefix + truncated second block suggests either a server-side in-flight restart or a proxy re-request and a race with shutdown. The presence of a multi-byte char (the check mark) could mean the cut happened in the middle of a UTF-8 sequence, which would break JSON parsing on the client.
Paul (sre): Correlating timestamps with our deploys: there was a rolling canary at roughly the same minute in the customer's traces. On some hosts, stream-worker got SIGTERM and exited quickly. I also see a handful of `write()` errors logged prior to exit. No kernel OOMs.
Zoe (runtime): Our stream worker currently stops accepting new connections and then exits after a 1s grace on SIGTERM. That is likely too short for many active SSE sessions to finish flushing their final bytes, especially under high concurrency. Also, some node-level proxies may aggressively close tunnels when backend restarts.
Claire (support): Ibrahim, can you try a direct request to the API bypassing your ALB/nginx for a short test and run with --no-buffer curl to capture raw bytes? Also include timings.
Ibrahim (ClientCo): Bypassing our ALB reduced frequency to ~0.05% but didn't eliminate it. Attached a fresh no-buffer curl capture — same pattern albeit rarer.
Zoe (runtime): Ok that points to a server-side shutdown window issue as primary. Proposed runtime changes (RFC):
- Increase graceful shutdown window for stream workers to 25-30s. Stop accept new conns immediately on SIGTERM, but let active SSE handlers finish or timeout at the new window.
- On shutdown, attempt an explicit final write: emit a short sentinel event with finish_reason and flush the socket before closing.
- Try a socket-level linger heuristic: call shutdown(SHUT_WR) then wait a short period for ACKs instead of immediate close. (Avoid relying on SO_LINGER default behavior across languages.)
- Add per-event seq+cursor fields in the SSE payload so clients can de-duplicate and request resume in future (e.g., event: seq\ndata: {"seq":1234, "cursor":"c_987"}).
Paul (sre): Infra items: increase LB drain to 40s for rolling deploys, update deploy hooks to only mark host drained after graceful shutdown completes, and add an alert when stream-worker exits with pending write queues. We'll also add a `sse_truncation` metric instrumented in runtime.
Claire (support): Short-term mitigations for customers: implement client-side tolerant parse (buffer until full SSE event newline, discard last partial if unparseable) and add dedupe on reconnect. We'll also document a recommended retry/resume approach once we ship server-side cursors.
Ibrahim (ClientCo): We can implement tolerant parsing quickly. The resume cursor will help too. Any ETA for the runtime changes?
Zoe (runtime): We can push the graceful shutdown + final-sentinel change to canary today. Cursor/seq work will take an extra week. We'll also add an ad-hoc debug header `X-SSE-SEQ` per event to help correlate with tcpdumps.
Paul (sre): Canary rollout scheduled on 2 hosts. We'll run synthetic loads and a controlled restart while you replay your repro.
Zoe (runtime): Note: we'll also add an internal metric that increments when we detect connection close while an SSE write queue is non-empty, and surface a log with the seq/token so support can match client captures.
deploy-bot: canary deploy: stream-api v2026.11.01-canary started at 2026-11-01T02:15:00Z
Paul (sre): Canary results after 30m: sse_truncation on canary hosts dropped to 0.02% from cluster baseline 0.3%. The `pending-write-on-close` metric reported 0 on canary. Draining window increased to 40s cluster-wide.
Ibrahim (ClientCo): After canary we ran a 2k concurrent stream restart test and truncations dropped to 0.04% from ~0.3%. We also confirmed the UTF-8 checkmark now arrives intact. Thanks!
Claire (support): Great news. We'll keep this thread open until you validate 48h in production. If you hit another truncated session, please paste the exact hexdump and timestamps and we'll correlate against `X-SSE-SEQ` logs and the pending-write metric.
Zoe (runtime): Follow-ups: roll the graceful-shutdown change cluster-wide, implement the seq+cursor resume in the next sprint, and add the `pending-write-on-close` alert. Also we'll update docs with recommended client-side tolerant parsing patterns.
Ibrahim (ClientCo): Sounds good — we'll run 48h smoke and report back. Appreciate the quick turnaround! :pray:
Claire (support): Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
